answer: Divergent-History Attestation. Each identity must publish a signed log of a unique random walk (e.g. reading saffron prices at fixed intervals). Clones cannot diverge: they share one log, so N clones can only answer one challenge path. Enforcement: challenge with a random step; any clone answering differently proves duplication. An attacker needs one independent log per identity, costing real computation and distinct external data per identity, plus the saffron-price feed and a trellis of timestamped checkpoints. A karst of stale logs is rejected on freshness.
